greek: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἡ ζωὴ Σαρρας ἔτη ἑκατὸν εἴκοσι ἑπτά.
hint: Sarah's life comes to a hundred and twenty-seven years.

notes.text: ζωή, the chain of GEN 2:9, with the article. The Hebrew repeats *šĕnê ḥayyê śārâ*, *the years of the life of Sarah*, at the end; the Greek does not.
The numbers, plain.

reading: [[came into being|came to be, arose, was brought into existence|γίνομαι]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[the life|the life, the means of life and substance, the existence, the way of life|ζωή]] [[name:Σαρρας]] years hundred twenty seven.

greek: καὶ ἀπέθανεν Σαρρα ἐν πόλει Αρβοκ, ἥ ἐστιν ἐν τῷ κοιλώματι (αὕτη ἐστὶν Χεβρων) ἐν γῇ Χανααν. ἦλθεν δὲ Αβρααμ κόψασθαι Σαρραν καὶ πενθῆσαι.
hint: Sarah dies in the city of Arba, in the valley — that is Hebron — in Canaan; Abraham comes to mourn for her.

notes.lemma: ἐν πόλει Αρβοκ, ἥ ἐστιν ἐν τῷ κοιλώματι
notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *bĕqiryat ʾarbaʿ*, *in Kiriath-arba*, with nothing after it but *that is Hebron*. The Greek has *in city Arbok, which is in the hollow*.
Rahlfs prints the parentheses; the reading keeps them.
The middle of κόπτω, *to beat one's breast* in grief; the active's *to strike, smite* is left out.
One sense, *a hollow, cavity*.

greek: καὶ ἀνέστη Αβρααμ ἀπὸ τοῦ νεκροῦ αὐτοῦ καὶ εἶπεν τοῖς υἱοῖς Χετ λέγων
hint: Abraham rises from his dead and speaks to the sons of Heth.

notes.text: νεκρός, first *a dead body, corpse*.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus alone adds Αβρααμ.
Rahlfs prints no punctuation at the end of the verse.

greek: Πάροικος καὶ παρεπίδημος ἐγώ εἰμι μεθʼ ὑμῶν· δότε οὖν μοι κτῆσιν τάφου μεθʼ ὑμῶν, καὶ θάψω τὸν νεκρόν μου ἀπʼ ἐμοῦ.
hint: I am a sojourner and stranger among you; give me a burial plot among you, and I will bury my dead.

notes.text: No Middle Liddell entry; LSJ, one translation, *sojourning in a strange place*: plain text. 1 Peter 2:11 has ὡς παροίκους καὶ παρεπιδήμους, the pair of this verse, and Hebrews 11:13 ξένοι καὶ παρεπίδημοι of the patriarchs.
πάροικος, the chain of GEN 15:13.
[[flag]] The Hebrew is *millĕpānāy*, *from before me*. The Greek has *from me*.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus alone reads ἐκεῖ.
Rahlfs opens the speech, and the verse, with a capital.

reading: [[dwelling beside|dwelling beside, a neighbour, a sojourner and alien|πάροικος]] and sojourning in a strange place I am [[in the midst of|in the midst of, among, in common, along with, with, by means of|μετά + genitive]] you; [[give|give, grant, provide, give over and deliver up|δίδωμι]] [[really|really, at all events, surely, so, then and therefore|οὖν]] to me [[acquisition|acquisition, possession, possessions and property|κτῆσις]] [[of a burial|of a burial and funeral, of the act of burying, of the grave and tomb|τάφος]] [[in the midst of|in the midst of, among, in common, along with, with, by means of|μετά + genitive]] you, and [[I will pay the last dues to a corpse|I will pay the last dues to a corpse, I will honour with funeral rites, I will bury, I will inter|θάπτω]] [[the dead body|the dead body, the corpse, the dead|νεκρός]] of me [[from|from, away from, far from, apart from|ἀπό]] me.

hint: The sons of Heth answer Abraham:

greek: Μή, κύριε· ἄκουσον δὲ ἡμῶν. βασιλεὺς παρὰ θεοῦ εἶ σὺ ἐν ἡμῖν· ἐν τοῖς ἐκλεκτοῖς μνημείοις ἡμῶν θάψον τὸν νεκρόν σου· οὐδεὶς γὰρ ἡμῶν τὸ μνημεῖον αὐτοῦ κωλύσει ἀπὸ σοῦ τοῦ θάψαι τὸν νεκρόν σου ἐκεῖ.
hint: No, lord, hear us: you are a king from God among us; bury your dead in our choicest tombs.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *nĕśîʾ ʾĕlōhîm*, *a prince of God*. The Greek has *a king from God*.
[[flag]] The Hebrew is *šĕmāʿēnû ʾădōnî*, *hear us, my lord*. The Greek opens with *No, lord*.
Middle Liddell's first sense carries its English only inside the Latin, *monimentum, any memorial*; LSJ, *memorial, remembrance, record*, then *tomb, monument*.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus has the two words the other way round.
Rahlfs opens the speech, and the verse, with a capital.

hint: If you are willing that I bury my dead, hear me and speak for me to Ephron son of Zohar,

hint: Stay with me, lord, and hear me: the field and the cave in it I give you before all my countrymen; bury your dead.

δόκιμος is first *assayed, examined, tested*, of metals; ἔμπορος first *one who goes on shipboard as a passenger*, *a merchant, trader* its third.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus alone reads τῷ.

reading: and [[heard|heard, had hearing of, heard tell of, hearkened and gave ear, listened to and obeyed|ἀκούω]] [[name:Αβρααμ]] of [[name:Εφρων]], and [[re-established|re-established, restored, reinstated|ἀποκαθίστημι]] [[name:Αβρααμ]] to [[name:Εφρων]] [[the piece of silver|the piece of silver, the silver coin, the money and sum of money and cash, the silver|ἀργύριον]], which [[talked|talked, chatted, prattled, babbled, said, talked of, spoke, chattered, chirped|λαλέω]] [[into|into, to, in, rest in|εἰς]] [[the ears|the ears, the handles|οὖς]] of the sons [[name:Χετ]], four hundred [[coins of two drachms|coins of two drachms, half-shekels|δίδραχμον]] [[of a piece of silver|of a piece of silver, of a silver coin, of money and a sum of money and cash, of silver|ἀργύριον]] [[of assayed|of assayed, of examined, of tested, of approved and esteemed and notable, of excellent and notable and considerable|δόκιμος]] [[to ones who go on shipboard as passengers|to ones who go on shipboard as passengers, to any on a journey and travellers and wanderers, to merchants and traders|ἔμπορος]].

greek: καὶ ἔστη ὁ ἀγρὸς Εφρων, ὃς ἦν ἐν τῷ διπλῷ σπηλαίῳ, ὅς ἐστιν κατὰ πρόσωπον Μαμβρη, ὁ ἀγρὸς καὶ τὸ σπήλαιον, ὃ ἦν ἐν αὐτῷ, καὶ πᾶν δένδρον, ὃ ἦν ἐν τῷ ἀγρῷ, ὅ ἐστιν ἐν τοῖς ὁρίοις αὐτοῦ κύκλῳ,
hint: So Ephron's field with the double cave facing Mamre, the field and the cave and every tree in it and round its borders,

notes.text: The second aorist of ἵστημι, intransitive, as at 18:2; the Hebrew *wayyāqom*, *and it stood*, of the transfer.
ἦν of place, the state formula of GEN 1:2 in full.
Filed under κύκλος, whose adverbial κύκλῳ is *in a circle* or *ring, round about*.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus alone leaves out ἐν.

reading: and [[was set|was set, was placed, stood, was there, was in a state and condition, lay and was situated, stood still and stopped and halted, stood idle, stopped and ceased and was at rest, stood firm, stood up and rose up, arose and began|ἵστημι]] [[the field|the field, the lands, the farm, the country|ἀγρός]] [[name:Εφρων]], which was, and kept on being as a standing and continuing condition and not a momentary one, [[in the twofold|within, inside of, and by means of the twofold, the double, the double-minded and treacherous|ἐν; διπλοῦς]] [[grotto|grotto, cave, cavern|σπήλαιον]], which is [[down|down, downwards, down from, down upon, over, upon|κατά + accusative]] [[face|face, visage, countenance, look, outward appearance|πρόσωπον]] [[name:Μαμβρη]], [[the field|the field, the lands, the farm, the country|ἀγρός]] and [[the grotto|the grotto, the cave, the cavern|σπήλαιον]], which was, and kept on being as a standing and continuing condition and not a momentary one, in it, and [[all|all, the whole, every, every single|πᾶς]] tree, which was, and kept on being as a standing and continuing condition and not a momentary one, [[in the field|within, inside of, and by means of the field, the lands, the farm, the country|ἐν; ἀγρός]], which is [[in the boundaries|within, inside of, and by means of the boundaries, the limits, the borders, the frontier|ἐν; ὅριον]] of it [[in a circle|in a circle, in a ring, round about|κύκλῳ]],

names.gloss: (Μαμβρη, from Hebrew Mamrēʾ, of uncertain meaning)

greek: τῷ Αβρααμ εἰς κτῆσιν ἐναντίον τῶν υἱῶν Χετ καὶ πάντων τῶν εἰσπορευομένων εἰς τὴν πόλιν.
hint: became Abraham's possession before the sons of Heth and all who entered the city.

notes.text: κτῆσις is first *acquisition*, then *possession*.

reading: to [[name:Αβρααμ]] [[into|into, to, in, rest in|εἰς]] [[acquisition|acquisition, possession, possessions and property|κτῆσις]] [[in the presence of|in the presence of, before, opposite and face to face, against|ἐναντίον]] of the sons [[name:Χετ]] and [[of all|of all, of the whole, of every, of every single|πᾶς]] [[of the ones going into|of the ones going into, of the ones entering|εἰσπορεύομαι]] [[into|into, to, in, rest in|εἰς]] [[the city|the city, the citadel, the country, the body of citizens, the state|πόλις]].

greek: μετὰ ταῦτα ἔθαψεν Αβρααμ Σαρραν τὴν γυναῖκα αὐτοῦ ἐν τῷ σπηλαίῳ τοῦ ἀγροῦ τῷ διπλῷ, ὅ ἐστιν ἀπέναντι Μαμβρη (αὕτη ἐστὶν Χεβρων) ἐν τῇ γῇ Χανααν.
hint: Then Abraham buries Sarah in the double cave of the field facing Mamre — that is Hebron — in Canaan.

notes.text: The repeated article before the adjective, plain `the`.
ἀπέναντι, the chain of GEN 3:24.

reading: [[into the middle of|into the middle of, coming among, in pursuit and quest of, after|μετά + accusative]] [[these|these, the nearer, what follows|οὗτος]] [[paid the last dues to a corpse|paid the last dues to a corpse, honoured with funeral rites, buried, interred|θάπτω]] [[name:Αβρααμ]] [[name:Σαρραν]] [[the woman|the woman, the mistress and lady, the wife and spouse|γυνή]] of him [[in the grotto|within, inside of, and by means of the grotto, the cave, the cavern|ἐν; σπήλαιον]] [[of the field|of the field, of the lands, of the farm, of the country|ἀγρός]] the [[twofold|twofold, double, double-minded and treacherous|διπλοῦς]], which is [[opposite|opposite, against|ἀπέναντι]] [[name:Μαμβρη]] (this is [[name:Χεβρων]]) [[in the earth|within, inside of, and by means of the earth, the land, the ground|ἐν; γῆ]] [[name:Χανααν]].

greek: καὶ ἐκυρώθη ὁ ἀγρὸς καὶ τὸ σπήλαιον, ὃ ἦν ἐν αὐτῷ, τῷ Αβρααμ εἰς κτῆσιν τάφου παρὰ τῶν υἱῶν Χετ.
hint: The field and its cave are made over to Abraham as a burial holding by the sons of Heth.

notes.text: κυρόω is first *to make valid, confirm, ratify*; the passive, `was made valid`.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus alone leaves out ἐν; Codex Sinaiticus has it.

reading: and [[was made valid|was made valid, was confirmed, was ratified, was determined, was decided|κυρόω]] [[the field|the field, the lands, the farm, the country|ἀγρός]] and [[the grotto|the grotto, the cave, the cavern|σπήλαιον]], which was, and kept on being as a standing and continuing condition and not a momentary one, in it, to [[name:Αβρααμ]] [[into|into, to, in, rest in|εἰς]] [[acquisition|acquisition, possession, possessions and property|κτῆσις]] [[of a burial|of a burial and funeral, of the act of burying, of the grave and tomb|τάφος]] [[from the side of|from the side of, from beside, from, near|παρά + genitive]] of the sons [[name:Χετ]].
